claims.claim_text: Joseph D Coppock is confirmed by a first-person Truman Library interview that explicitly describes his late-1943 move into OSS and later naval commission.
claims.evidence_excerpt: So in late 1943, I went to the OSS (Office of Strategic Services), first on a civilian basis.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact-name interviewee describes his own OPA-to-OSS chronology and says OSS arranged his early-1944 naval commission as a lieutenant junior grade.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed. The distinctive exact full name and explicit first-person OSS service statement directly identify the indexed person.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source explicitly dates civilian OSS entry to late 1943 and the naval commission to early 1944.
claims.match_notes: The index has no printed rank or identifier for Coppock. The personnel category reflects his documented later OSS-arranged naval commission while preserving his initial civilian OSS status in the claim text.
